parts.text: While playing with her friends in their school playground, Katelyn saw 500 fairies flying above the nearby forest.
After about twenty minutes, one of her friends saw half as many fairies as Katelyn saw come from the east and join the fairies that were there.
Ten minutes later, 300 fairies flew away.

items.question: While playing with her friends in their school playground, Katelyn saw 500 fairies flying above the nearby forest. After about twenty minutes, one of her friends saw half as many fairies as Katelyn saw come from the east and join the fairies that were there. Ten minutes later, 300 fairies flew away. How many fairies are remaining?

parts.text: Mr. Hezekiah had 20 trucks from his store supplying fertiliser to different farmers in his hometown dispatched for delivery on a particular day.
Each truck was carrying 20 tons of fertiliser packed in bags.

Two hours after the trucks had departed for delivery, Mr Hezekiah got the news that a quarter of the number of lorries dispatched for delivery had mechanical failures on the road and could not deliver the fertilisers to the farmers.

At the same time, he also received a report that 5 of his trucks had been caught in a heavy rainstorm, but luckily the waterproof covers on the trucks protected the fertiliser from getting wet and did not affect the delivery.
Calculate the total number of tons of fertiliser that reached the farmers that day?

parts.text: One dwarf can mine some ore per day with his bare hands.
He can mine twice as much with an iron pickaxe and 50% more with a steel pickaxe than with an iron pickaxe.
If 40 dwarves with steel pickaxes mine for a month with 30 days and produced 43200 pounds of ore, how many pounds of ore can one dwarf mine per day with his bare hands?

parts.text: Joe has twice as many cars as Robert.
He sells 30% of them and gives away twice as many cars as the number he sold to his mother.
If Robert has 15 cars, how many cars does Joe remain with after selling and giving some to his mother?

parts.text: Jessica is trying to figure out how much to pay on all her debts each month.
Her student loans have a minimum payment of $300/month, her credit card's minimum is $200/month, and her mortgage's minimum is $500/month.
She also subscribes to Netflix for $15 a month, but she has a coupon to offset that $15.
If Jessica wants to pay 50% more than the minimum on her debts and continues to pay the regular amount for her gym and Netflix, how much does she pay for her debts in a year?
